title: The Global Imaginary
description: The concept of the global imaginary poses a challenge to the methodological and discursive approaches to globalization in dominant social science disciplines. Evoking the imaginary offers an opportunity to move beyond the material descriptions of globalization and substantially consider what some describe as “disembodied globalization,” that is the words, images, texts, symbols, ideas, narratives and aesthetic forms of expression that point to a developing global consciousness. This course examines the work of thinkers who grapple with the notion of the imaginary and contribute to an understanding of the subjective and affective dimensions of imagining and experiencing our interconnected world through a global perspective.

title: Literature of Globalization and Globality
description: Globalization is reflected thematically in works of literature. However, an examination of the process and dynamics of globalization through a literary perspective offers more than the treatment of globalization as a theme. This course explores the intersection of literature and globalization by raising the following questions: What is a literary approach to globalization and what are its literary registers? How do writers contribute to the discursive construction of globalization in their novels? How do literary texts represent experiences of globalization? What does it mean to write the global? We will engage these questions while reading novels by writers who offer narrativizations of globalization and express visions of globality.

title: What is Global Studies?
description: Basic to global studies is connectivity, over different periods and phases. Hegemony is convergence on one center. Making way for multicentrism and multilateralism, the opposite of hegemony, is a leading theme of the 21st century. It unfolds in geoeconomics, geopolitics, finance, innovation and technology. Asia and China lead in several spheres. Approaches in this course are multidisciplinary and include comparative studies.

title: Globalization/Trump
description: For the US the honeymoon with globalization is over. Trump is part of the response. Russell Vought (Project 2025) heads the White House Office of Management and Budget with plans to drastically cut Medicare and Social Security. When the center doesn’t hold realignments follow. White supremacy means retribution for critics of DJ Trump and Democrats. Trump 1.0 represented populism, Trump 2.0 represents authoritarianism. Questions: Is the problem Trump or the US? Is Trump’s journey part of American decline? Is blaming China the way forward for the US? What are the agendas of billionaires? Just political economy or also culture? Is what is on the table American culture or also American civilization? Another world is already in the making.

title: Law in Global Context
description: This course deals with current global issues and the legal consequences that transcend borders of nation-states, including human rights, environment, conflict, religion, criminal activities, terrorism, the Internet, and disease.

title: Global Environmental Law & Policy
description: Global environmental problems in our time, particularly climate change and its impact on resource scarcity, human security, energy geopolitics, and democracy in an unevenly structured world system, including the search for world order solutions.

title: Teaching Assistant Practicum
description: Analyses of texts and materials, discussion of teaching techniques, conducting discussion sections, formulation of topics and questions for papers and examinations, and grading papers and examinations under the supervision of the instructor. Designed to meet the needs of the graduate student who serves as a teaching assistant.
prerequisites_raw: Appointment as teaching assistant in Global and International Studies.
